contexts.text: He embraced him () = affection... That embracing pertains to affection in general, is known.

And embraced him () = the first conjunction of love. To embrace = affection... That to embrace is an effect, because it flows from the conjunction of love, is evident... Thus in the internal sense it is this conjunction.
To fall on the neck = a closer conjunction; for it is a closer embrace.

He kissed them = conjunction from the affection of truth... because it follows that he embraced them (), by which is signified conjunction from the affection of good; for to embrace = a more interior and consequently a closer affection than to kiss.

To embrace = the conjunction of love, thus conjunction from the affection of good. That to embrace = this affection, is clearly evident from the testification of love by embracing: embracing is an act which flows therefrom; for every spiritual affection has a bodily gesture which corresponds to itself, and which gesture is its representative.
They most tenderly embraced each other.
The acts (of love truly conjugial) as kissing, embracing, etc... delight the Third Heaven; for that Heaven is in the communication of good affections.
